name: French lessons
about: The path through the first French words, a few at a time, each in everyday sentences written for its lesson. Word list: FrequencyWords by Hermit Dave, from OpenSubtitles (opensubtitles.org), CC BY-SA 4.0.

words.le: the; him, her, it as an object pronoun
words.rentrer: to go or come back home
words.chercher: to look for; to fetch, to get after aller
words.connaître: to know a person or thing
words.toi: you (after a preposition, or on its own)
words.en: in, by; some, of it as a pronoun
words.question: question
words.poser: to put; to ask a question
words.prendre: to take; to have food or drink
words.sortir: to go out; to take out
words.asseoir: to seat; s'asseoir = to sit down
words.moi: me (after a preposition or on its own)
words.apporter: to bring, to take something to someone
words.manquer: to be missed; manquer à quelqu'un = to be missed by someone
words.réussir: to succeed; réussir à = to manage to
words.régler: to sort out, take care of
words.raison: reason; being right in avoir raison
words.dont: relative link for de; in the way that
words.occuper: to take care of with se and de
words.quitter: to leave a place or person
words.calmer: to calm; se calmer = to calm down
words.souvenir: to remember with se souvenir de
words.reculer: to step back, to move back
words.profiter: to enjoy, to make the most of

s-il-vous-plait.about: Literally if it pleases you: to someone you say vous to, as in a café.

bonjour.about: Literally good day: the everyday hello, morning to early evening.

ca-va.about: Literally that goes: the everyday way to ask, and Ça va is the answer too.

c-est.about: ce est, run together: it's or that's.

qu-est-ce-que.about: Literally what is it that: the everyday way to start a question with what.

en-voiture.about: Says how someone travels, without an article before voiture.

vite-fait.about: A familiar way to ask for a short, quick action.

il-y-a.about: Introduces something that is there; a stays the same with one thing or several.

quelque-chose.about: These two words together mean something.

pres-de.about: Says where someone or something is, near another person or thing.

s-il-te-plait.about: To one person you say tu to; s'il vous plaît is polite or plural.

ce-que.about: Introduces what someone says or does inside a statement or question.

a-pied.about: aller or rentrer à pied means go or come home on foot: walk.

chez-toi.en: at your place, to your house
chez-toi.about: To your house after venir; the forms themselves are explained at lesson 27.

vas-y.about: A familiar invitation to go ahead, addressed to tu.

au-travail.about: The contraction au is explained with au bureau in lesson 40.

de-nouveau.about: An action happens again, for instance when a phone connection comes back.

pardon.about: Used when you haven't heard or understood, or to apologize.

avoir-l-air.about: avoir l'air plus an adjective says how something seems.

bien-sur.about: A natural way to agree or grant permission.

en-retard.about: être en retard means to be late for an expected time.

en-conge.about: être en congé means to have time off work.

apres-manger.about: The infinitive manger follows après in this everyday expression.

tout-le-monde.about: The expression means everyone and takes a singular verb.

jusqu-a-ce-que.about: Introduces the event waited for; its verb takes the subjunctive.

non-plus.about: Goes with a negative statement: Je ne sais pas tout non plus.

ma-puce.about: An affectionate way to address a child; literally my flea.

il-n-y-a.about: The negative form of il y a; personne here completes the negative meaning: nobody.

quand-meme.about: Marks something unexpected or contrary to what was expected.

qu-est-ce-qui.about: Asks what is the subject of the following action.

au-sujet-de.about: Introduces what someone is talking about.

quoi-que-ce-soit.about: Used after the negative here: no need to do anything.

pas-du-tout.about: Strengthens a negative; keep ne before the conjugated verb.

mais-si.about: Contradicts a negative suggestion: Mais si, j'aime le café.

tout-de-suite.about: Says that something happens without delay.

jeter-un-coup-d-oeil.about: An everyday expression for looking briefly.

a-cette-epoque.about: Points to a time in the past.

il-y-a-un-an.about: Here il y a dates a past event, rather than introducing something present.

c-est-pourquoi.about: Introduces the result of what was just explained.

au-fait.about: Introduces a new point in the conversation.

de-long-en-large.about: Used with marcher for pacing back and forth.

prendre-soin.about: Prendre soin de means take care of someone or something.

prends-soin.about: The familiar command: prends soin de toi, take care of yourself.

donne-toi.about: A familiar command: the pronoun follows the verb with a hyphen.

un-jour.about: An unspecified day in the future.

en-train-de.about: After être, en train de plus an infinitive stresses an action in progress.

pendant-que.about: Introduces another action or situation happening at the same time.

en-haut.about: In a house, en haut means upstairs.

avant-que.about: Introduces a clause with the subjunctive.

n-est-ce-pas.about: A short question asking for confirmation.

a-l-envers.about: Says that something has the wrong orientation.

en-lisant.about: En with the present participle of lire: reading at the same time as the main action.

en-mangeant.about: En with the present participle of manger: eating at the same time as the main action.

en-marchant.about: En with the present participle of marcher: walking at the same time as the main action.

pas-mal.about: Pas mal means quite a lot in this affirmative expression.

n-y-etre-pour-rien.about: With tu, tu n'y es pour rien says that something is not your fault.

en-bas.about: In a house, en bas means downstairs.

pour-que.about: Introduces a purpose with its own subject and a verb in the subjunctive.

au-moins.about: Sets a minimum or points out something positive.

en-tout-cas.about: Introduces what remains true whatever else happens.

au-courant.about: Être au courant means to know about what is being discussed.

faire-attention.about: The familiar command fais attention asks someone to take care.

a-ce-rythme.about: Introduces the likely result if things continue this way.

en-colere.about: Être en colère means to be angry; contre introduces the person you are angry with.

du-moins.about: Narrows or qualifies what was just said.

n-importe-quoi.about: After c'est, a familiar way to dismiss something as nonsense.

un-pas.about: Pas can name a step; here it is a noun, not part of a negative.

Mais si, j'ai réfléchi à cette choix.

Mais si, elle est déjà revenus.

Ce sont absolument de bêtises.

items.text: Mais si, ça change beaucoup de choses.

wrong: Mais si, ça changent beaucoup de choses.
Mais si, ça change beaucoup de chose.

Tu es sortis aujourd'hui?

J'étais malades hier.

Nous sommes déjà allés chez les médecin.

Tu as passé une bon journée?

Elle a eu très mauvais.

Nous n'avons pas eu la temps.

Je ne me sentait pas bien hier.

items.text: Comment tu te sentais après la discussion?

Comment tu te sentais après le discussion?

Nous nous sentions en sécurité chez tu.

items.text: Je me sens en sécurité pendant la journée.
items.means: I feel safe during the day.

Je me sens en sécurité pendant le journée.

Le journée a été longue, mais nous sommes en sécurité.

items.means: The witness saw the man escape.
wrong: Le témoin a vu le homme s'échapper.
Le témoin a vu l'homme se échapper.

items.means: Has the witness seen the man?
wrong: Le témoin a voir l'homme?
Le témoin a vu le homme?

Selon le témoin, il n'est pas coupables.

items.text: Pourquoi tu te sens coupable?
items.means: Why do you feel guilty?
wrong: Pourquoi tu sens te coupable?
Pourquoi tu te sens coupables?

items.text: Je t'ai pardonné.
items.means: I've forgiven you.
wrong: Je te ai pardonné.
Je t'ai pardonner.

items.text: Tu peux me pardonner un jour?
items.means: Can you ever forgive me?
wrong: Tu peux pardonner me un jour?
Tu peux me pardonnes un jour?

items.text: Je te pardonne, mais je n'oublierai pas.

wrong: Je pardonne te, mais je n'oublierai pas.
Je te pardonne, mais je ne oublierai pas.

items.means: The man wants to escape from prison.

L'homme veut se échapper de prison.

items.means: The witness said that the man had escaped.
wrong: Le témoin a dit que le homme s'était échappé.
Le témoin a dit que l'homme se était échappé.

items.text: L'accident, c'est ma faute.
items.means: The accident is my fault.
wrong: Le accident, c'est ma faute.
L'accident, c'est mon faute.

items.means: Why are you crying?
wrong: Pourquoi tu pleure?
Pourquoi te pleures?

items.means: I heard you crying.
wrong: Je te ai entendu pleurer.
Je t'ai entendu pleures.

otherGender.text: Je t'ai entendue pleurer.

items.text: Ça doit être terrible pour toi.
items.means: That must be terrible for you.
wrong: Ça doit es terrible pour toi.
Ça doit être terrible pour tu.

items.text: Nous avons pu parler de nos sentiments.
items.means: We were able to talk about our feelings.
wrong: Nous avons pu parlons de nos sentiments.
Nous avons pu parler de notre sentiments.

items.text: Je peux t'offrir de l'aide?
items.means: Can I offer you some help?
wrong: Je peux te offrir de l'aide?
Je peux t'offrir de le aide?

items.text: Nous avons pu lui offrir de l'aide.
items.means: We were able to offer help to her.
wrong: Nous avons pu offrir lui de l'aide.
Nous avons pu lui offrir de le aide.

items.text: C'est terrible de te voir comme ça.
items.means: It's terrible to see you like this.
wrong: C'est terrible de voir te comme ça.
Ce est terrible de te voir comme ça.

items.text: Je ne veux pas te faire pleurer.
items.means: I don't want to make you cry.
wrong: Je ne veux pas faire te pleurer.
Je ne veux pas te faire pleures.

items.text: Tu peux me parler de tes sentiments; je veux t'offrir mon aide.
items.means: You can tell me about your feelings; I want to offer you my help.
wrong: Tu peux parler me de tes sentiments; je veux t'offrir mon aide.
Tu peux me parler de tes sentiments; je veux t'offrir ma aide.

items.text: Après cette terrible soirée, je comprends tes sentiments.
items.means: After that terrible evening, I understand your feelings.
wrong: Après ce terrible soirée, je comprends tes sentiments.
Après cette terrible soirée, je comprends ton sentiments.

items.text: Il n'y a rien de mal à avoir ces sentiments.
items.means: There's nothing wrong with having these feelings.
wrong: Il n'y a rien de mal à avoir cette sentiments.
Il n'y a rien de mal à avoir ces sentiment.

items.text: Le cheval ne veut pas sauter.
items.means: The horse doesn't want to jump.
wrong: Le cheval ne veut pas saute.
La cheval ne veut pas sauter.

items.text: Tu as vu le cheval sauter?
items.means: Did you see the horse jump?
wrong: Tu as vu la cheval sauter?
Tu as vu le cheval saute?

items.text: Ne saute pas dans l'eau!
items.means: Don't jump into the water!
wrong: Ne saute pas dans le eau!
Ne sautes pas dans l'eau!

items.text: Nous faisons un feu.
items.means: We're making a fire.
wrong: Nous faisons une feu.
Nous faisons un feux.

items.text: J'ai vu le feu.
items.means: I saw the fire.
wrong: Je ai vu le feu.
J'ai vu la feu.

items.text: Elle protège son enfant avec son corps.
items.means: She's shielding her child with her body.
wrong: Elle protège son enfant avec sa corps.
Elle protèges son enfant avec son corps.

items.text: Nous avons pu sauver le cheval.
items.means: We were able to save the horse.
wrong: Nous avons pu sauvons le cheval.
Nous avons pu sauver la cheval.

items.text: Reste à côté du feu, il fait froid.
items.means: Stay by the fire, it's cold.
wrong: Reste à côté de le feu, il fait froid.
Reste à côté du feu, il fait froide.

items.text: Le cheval a été sauvé par mon frère.
items.means: The horse was saved by my brother.
wrong: Le cheval a été sauvée par mon frère.
Le cheval a été sauvé par ma frère.

items.text: Il faisait froid quand nous avons sauvé ce cheval.
items.means: It was cold when we saved that horse.
wrong: Il faisait froid quand nous avons sauvé cette cheval.
Il faisait froide quand nous avons sauvé ce cheval.

items.text: On a sauvé le cheval du feu.
items.means: We saved the horse from the fire.
wrong: On a sauvé le cheval de le feu.
On a sauvé la cheval du feu.

items.means: Can you tell us your story?
wrong: Tu peux raconter nous ton histoire?
Tu peux nous racontes ton histoire?

items.text: Elle a déjà raconté cette histoire?
items.means: Has she told that story already?
wrong: Elle a déjà raconter cette histoire?
Elle a déjà raconté ce histoire?

items.text: Nous nous sommes raconté des histoires.
items.means: We told each other stories.
wrong: Nous nous sommes racontés des histoires.
Nous nous sommes raconté des histoire.

items.text: La fête était fantastique.
items.means: The party was fantastic.
wrong: Le fête était fantastique.
La fête était fantastiques.

items.text: J'ai lu un livre fantastique.
items.means: I've read a fantastic book.
wrong: Je ai lu un livre fantastique.
J'ai lu un livre fantastiques.

items.text: Ça a l'air fantastique!
items.means: That sounds fantastic!
wrong: Ça a le air fantastique!
Ça a l'air fantastiques!

items.means: I'm proud of you.
wrong: Je suis fier de tu.
Je suis fiers de toi.

items.means: You can be proud of yourself.
wrong: Tu peux es fier de toi.
Tu peux être fier de tu.

otherGender.text: Tu peux être fière de toi.

items.text: Nous sommes fiers de notre équipe.
items.means: We're proud of our team.
wrong: Nous sommes fier de notre équipe.
Nous sommes fiers de nos équipe.

items.text: J'aurais aimé raconter cette histoire à ma mère.
items.means: I would have liked to tell this story to my mother.
wrong: Je aurais aimé raconter cette histoire à ma mère.
J'aurais aimé raconter cette histoire à mon mère.

words.means: du, de l' = some (English often says nothing)
a lot; beaucoup de = a lot of

lessons.title: Find the phone on the table

concept.line: Every noun is a le word or a la word: le téléphone, la table. Learn which with the word.
Raise your voice at the end to ask, or start with a question word: Où est la voiture? (where is the car?)

words.means: es = are (with tu); n'est = isn't (ne and est run together)

concept.line: mon goes before a le word and ma before a la word: mon téléphone, ma clé (my phone, my key). Before a la word starting with a vowel sound it's mon too: mon eau.

words.means: a = has; n'a = hasn't, doesn't have; n'ai = haven't, don't have
de = of (le livre de ma mère: my mother's book)

concept.line: du goes with le words, de la with la words, and de l' before a vowel: du café, du lait, de l'eau. English often says nothing: Je bois du café (I drink coffee). After ne … pas, what you don't have, drink or eat takes de: Je n'ai pas de lait; after être it stays: Ce n'est pas du thé.

words.means: vient = comes; viens = come (with je, tu)
to; at: à la maison = home, at home

concept.line: ne goes before the verb and pas after it: Je ne bois pas de café (I don't drink coffee). Before a vowel, ne becomes n': Elle n'est pas ici.

words.means: veux = want (with je, tu); voulons = want (with nous); veut = wants
manger = to eat; mangeons = eat (with nous); manges = eat (with tu)
boire = to drink; buvons = drink (with nous)

concept.line: After vouloir, the next verb stays in its basic form, the one ending in -er, -ir or -re: Je veux manger (I want to eat), Tu veux boire un café?
The verb changes with who does it: je mange, tu manges, il mange, nous mangeons. Many of the forms sound alike and are spelled apart.

words.means: peux = can (with je, tu); pouvons = can (with nous)
vais = go (with je); allez = go (with vous); aller = to go
you (polite; or to more than one)
sais = know (with je, tu); savez = know (with vous)
ce = this, that (before a le word); cette = this, that (before a la word)

concept.line: vous is the polite you, for someone you don't know well, and you to more than one person. Its verb usually ends in -ez (vous êtes is the big exception): Vous savez où c'est? (you know where it is?)
ce goes before a le word and cette before a la word, for this or that: ce livre, cette clé. Before a le word that starts with a vowel, ce becomes cet, so never cet livre.

lessons.title: I still have work to do

words.means: dois = have to, must (with je, tu); devons = have to (with nous)
travailler = to work; travaille = work, works
rentrons = we go home; rentres = you go home
marche = I walk; marchons = we walk
aider = to help; aide = helps; j'aide = I help
peut = can (with il, elle or a person)
cherche = I look for; cherchons = we look for; cherchent = they look for
venons = come (with nous); viennent = come (with ils or two people)
heures = hours; deux heures = two o'clock

concept.line: je voudrais means I'd like, a politer way to ask than je veux (I want): Je voudrais un rendez-vous.

words.means: payer = to pay; paie = I pay
n'as = don't have (ne and as run together)
vois = see (with je, tu); voir = to see; voyons = we see
what (at the end of a question)
connais = know (with je, tu); connaissons = we know

concept.line: qui asks who, que or quoi what, où where, comment how, quand when and combien how much. Qu'est-ce que starts a what question; quoi can go at the end: Tu vois quoi? Keep the ordinary subject and verb order in Comment je peux aider?

words.means: j'habite = I live; habite = lives; habites = you live
in; en ville = in town, in the city
we (with the il form of the verb)
prépare = prepares, gets (a meal) ready; préparer = to prepare
aime = like, likes (with je, il, elle or on)
faites = do, make (with vous); fait = does, makes (with il, elle or on)

concept.line: In everyday French, on can mean we. Its verb has the il form: On fait du café (we're making coffee), On mange ensemble (we eat together).

words.means: besoin = need; avoir besoin de = to need
appeler = to call; appelez = call (polite); appelle = call (to a friend)
reste = I stay; restez = you stay (with vous)
poser = to ask (a question); pose = ask (to a friend)
you (as the object, before the verb)
t'aider = to help you (te and aider run together)
rester = to stay; restes = stay (with tu)
attendons = we wait; attendre = to wait; attendez = you wait; j'attends = I wait; t'attend = waits for you (te and attend run together)
t'entend = hears you; t'entends = hear you; m'entendre = to hear me; m'entends = hear me; m'entendez = hear me (with vous); t'entendre = to hear you (te and entendre run together)
m'aider = to help me (me and aider run together)

concept.line: me is the person heard or helped, and goes before its verb: Tu m'entends? (can you hear me?). Before a vowel, me becomes m'. With peux, put it before the infinitive: Tu peux m'aider? (can you help me?).

words.means: sert = serves (with il, elle or on)
attends = wait (to one person you say tu to)
acheter = to buy; achètes = you buy; achetons = we buy; j'achète = I buy; n'achetons = don't buy (ne and achetons run together)
rentre = comes or goes home (with il or elle)
commences = you start; commence = I start, starts
comprends = understand (with je, tu); comprenez = understand (with vous)

lessons.title: A busy day at the office

words.means: au = to the, at the (à and le run together)
dormir = to sleep; dors = sleep (with je or tu)
doit = has to (with il, elle or on)

concept.line: car gives a reason after a statement: Je reste au lit, car je veux dormir. The subject stays before its verb. car is more common in writing than parce que, which comes later.

words.means: prends = take (with je or tu); prend = takes; prendre = to take
j'en = I ... some, of it (before a verb)
ai = have (with je, with another word between them)

concept.line: After ne ... pas, du, de la and an indefinite un or une usually become de: Je n'ai pas de café. Before a vowel, de becomes d': pas d'argent. With être, the article stays: Ce n'est pas du café.

words.means: pense = think (with je); penses = think (with tu)
qu'il = that he (que and il run together)
qu'elle = that she (que and elle run together)

concept.line: que links what you think to a full statement: Je pense que nous pouvons manger ici. Keep the subject before its verb. Before il, que becomes qu': Je pense qu'il est à la maison.

words.means: suit = follows (with il, elle or a noun)
sors = go out (with je or tu)
promener = to walk someone; me promène, te promènes = go for a walk
se = oneself; se promener = to go for a walk
mettre = to put; mets = put (with je or tu); met = puts
raconter = to tell a story; raconte-lui = tell him or her
son, sa = his or her (agreeing with the thing named)
lui = to him or her (before a verb)
l'aider = to help her or him

concept.line: French has no fixed time-before-place rule. Je reste à la maison ce soir and Ce soir, je reste à la maison are both natural. The subject stays before its verb when the time comes first.

words.means: regarder = to watch; regarde = watch (with je)
amusante = fun, entertaining (with a feminine noun)
n'aime = don't like (with je); aimes = like (with tu)
entre = come in (to one person you say tu to)

lessons.title: Spending a day off at home

words.means: time off work; un jour de congé = a day off
qu'on = that we (que and on run together)

concept.line: parce que gives the reason for something. Keep the ordinary subject and verb order: Je reste à la maison parce que je suis en congé. car also gives a reason; parce que is the usual everyday choice.

words.means: donne = give (with je); donne-moi = give me (to one familiar person)
parler = to talk; parle = talk, talks
appelle-moi = call me (to one familiar person)
rentrer = to go or come home
pris = taken (after avoir); prendre une photo = to take a photo

concept.line: Use avoir and a past participle to say what happened: J'ai travaillé, Tu as appelé. This can mean I worked or I have worked. Here the regular -er verbs have a participle in -é: travaillé, appelé.

lessons.title: What did you have for lunch?

concept.line: Learn each past participle with its verb: mangé, bu, lu, vu, acheté. avoir changes for the subject: Tu as bu; Nous avons bu. The participle follows avoir.

words.means: allé = gone (after être, with a masculine singular subject)
venue = come (after être, with a feminine singular subject)
rentré = come home (after être, with a masculine singular subject)
resté, restés = stayed (after être, masculine singular or plural)
attendu = waited (after avoir); m'attends = wait for me; attend = waits

concept.line: aller, venir, rentrer and rester use être for the past here. The participle matches the subject: Je suis allé for a man, Je suis allée for a woman; Elle est venue. attendre takes avoir: J'ai attendu.

words.means: j'écoute = I listen; n'écoutes = do not listen (with tu); écouter = to listen

concept.line: Learn the link with the French verb. attendre and écouter take the thing or person directly: attendre le médecin, écouter la musique. penser à takes à; parler de takes de. English for or to does not automatically become pour or à.

words.means: assis, assise = sat down (after être, with me or se)
s'est = se and est joined (in a past action)

concept.line: Many adjectives follow their noun, as in une porte ouverte. beau is one of the common ones that go before: une belle maison, un beau quartier. Before a masculine noun starting with a vowel sound, use bel: un bel endroit.

words.means: sortis = gone out (after être); sortons = go out (with nous)
prêts = ready (for a masculine or mixed group)
s'appelle = is called (se and appelle joined)

lessons.title: Taking a book to your brother

words.means: apporter = to bring, take something; j'apporte = I bring
m'asseoir = to sit down (referring to je)
demander = to ask, to ask for
connaît = knows (with il, elle or a singular noun)
mal = pain, hurt (in avoir mal and faire mal)
forte = strong, intense (with a feminine noun)

lessons.title: Asking someone to put a book here

words.means: jette = throw; jette-moi = throw me; jeter = to throw
donne-le-moi = give it to me (to one familiar person)

concept.line: Before the verb, me or te comes before le or la: Je te le donne. In a positive instruction the pronouns follow with hyphens, and me becomes moi: Donne-le-moi. A negative instruction puts them before the verb again: Ne me le donne pas.

words.means: t'arrêter = to stop (referring to tu); arrêter = to stop
venu = come (after être, with a masculine singular subject)
sûr = certain; c'est sûr = that's for sure
failli = almost did (after avoir, before an infinitive)
t'ai = te and ai joined (with je)
apprendre = to learn; appris = learned or taught (after avoir)
the right; avoir le droit de = to be allowed to
rentrée = returned home (after être, with a feminine singular subject)
sort = comes out; sortie = come out (after être, feminine)
attendue = waited for (matching a feminine direct object before avoir)
dire = to say; vouloir dire = to mean
utiliser = to use; l'utiliser = to use it
l'essayer = to try it (le and essayer joined)
what, which (before a masculine singular noun)
quelques = a few (before a plural noun)
ces = these, those (before a plural noun)
sont = are (with ils, elles or plural nouns)
parlent = talk, are about (with plural subjects)

concept.line: For more than one, write livres and photos with -s; the ending is normally silent. Use les for the, des for some and ces for these or those. Adjectives also match: de belles photos. Before a preceding plural adjective, indefinite des normally becomes de.

en refers back to the things or amount already being discussed. Put it before the verb and keep the number or amount: J'en ai deux; J'en ai assez. With an infinitive, en goes before that infinitive: Je vais en prendre deux.

words.means: passons = go through (with nous); passes = go through (with tu); passés = gone through
m'as = me and as joined (with tu)
rentrés = returned home (after être, masculine or mixed plural)

concept.line: Learn the link with the expression: essayer de dormir, apprendre à conduire, sans danger de marcher. pour + infinitive gives a purpose: aller en ville pour acheter quelque chose. After vouloir, pouvoir or devoir, the infinitive has no linking preposition.

lessons.title: Meeting someone for the first time

words.means: rencontre = meet (with je); rencontres = meet (with tu)
manque = is missed; tu nous manques = we miss you
buvions = used to drink, were drinking
habitait = used to live, was living
se passe = happens (il se passe quelque chose: something is happening)

lessons.title: Keeping in touch during a busy week

words.means: vus = seen, for more than one
appelés = called, for more than one
eux = them, for contrast or after a preposition
change, changent = changes, change (one thing; several)

concept.line: moi, toi, lui, elle, nous, vous and eux can stand alone or mark a contrast. With a reinforced subject, keep the ordinary subject pronoun too: Toi, tu viens? Moi, non. After a preposition use the same tonic forms: avec toi, avec eux.

words.means: sens, sent = feel (je sens, tu sens; il, elle sent)

concept.line: To say how someone feels, use se sentir with the pronoun that matches the subject: Je me sens fort, Tu te sens fort, Elle se sent forte. To feel a part of your body, sentir takes it directly: Je sens mon bras.

words.means: envoie-moi = send me (to tu); t'envoie = send you (je t'envoie); envoyer = to send
tire = pull (je tire; Tire! to tu); tirer = to pull
se débloque = comes free; débloquée = unstuck
réussi = managed (j'ai réussi à: I managed to)
laisse-moi = leave me, let me (to tu); laisse = leave (je te laisse: I'll leave you)
ne t'inquiète pas = don't worry (to tu)
réglé = sorted out, taken care of (after j'ai, tu as…)
explique, expliques = explain (Explique! to tu; tu expliques); expliqué = explained (after j'ai)

concept.line: Inside another sentence, keep the question word and ordinary subject-verb order: Je sais où tu habites. Use si for whether and ce que for what someone says or does. The embedded question is a clause inside the larger sentence.

In these sentences, mais adds surprise, donc encourages someone, quand même marks something unexpected and bien softens aimer. Their English depends on the sentence: Mais pourquoi tu as peur? is Why on earth are you scared? Appelle donc ton père is Go on, call your dad.

words.means: ressemble, ressemblent, ressemblons à = look like (il, elle; ils; nous)
dirait = would say; on dirait = it looks as if

concept.line: The simple future uses a future stem plus -ai, -as, -a, -ons, -ez or -ont: Je t'appellerai demain. Nous resterons means we'll stay. Aller plus an infinitive also talks about plans: Je vais appeler ta mère demain.

words.means: dont = in which, after la façon

words.means: m'occupe = take care; je m'occupe de = I take care of

concept.line: The conditional uses the future stem with -ais, -ais, -ait, -ions, -iez, -aient: pourrais, serais, pourrions. It expresses would or could and softens requests. For an imagined condition, use si plus the imperfect, then the conditional: Si j'avais le temps, je pourrais t'aider.

The imperfect describes a past situation or habit; the passé composé presents a completed event. J'étais petit describes how I was; J'ai appelé names a completed call. Most imperfect stems come from the present nous form without -ons, with -ais, -ais, -ait, -ions, -iez, -aient; être uses ét-.

concept.line: The present can mean am doing. Être en train de plus an infinitive stresses an action happening right now: Je suis en train de travailler.

concept.line: Learn the link with the expression: difficile à comprendre, oublier de téléphoner, avant de rentrer. Keep the next verb in its infinitive. Pour plus an infinitive gives a purpose.

concept.line: Si introduces a condition: si tu veux. An imagined condition uses si plus the imperfect and a conditional outcome. For future events, quand takes the future: quand je serai à la maison.

concept.line: En plus an -ant form joins two actions done by the same person at the same time: Je mange en lisant. Ordinary present forms can also describe what someone is doing.

concept.line: The imperfect of avoir or être plus a past participle says what had happened before another past moment: J'avais déjà mangé. Keep the usual auxiliary and agreement: Il était déjà rentré.

concept.line: Use avoir with pu, dû or voulu, then an infinitive: On a pu ouvrir la porte; J'ai dû partir; Mon fils n'a pas voulu manger. Pu says someone managed to, dû that they had to, and n'a pas voulu that they refused.

concept.line: Use être with a past participle to say what is done to someone or something. The participle agrees with the subject: La porte a été ouverte. Par introduces who does it: Ce livre est lu par mon père.

concept.line: Use plus, moins or aussi before an adjective, then que for the comparison: plus grande que, moins grande que, aussi grande que. Bon becomes meilleur. To choose the greatest in a group, use the agreeing article: la maison la plus grande.

concept.line: Use plus, moins or aussi ... que to compare. Bon becomes meilleur, with agreement; bien becomes mieux. Plus tôt and plus tard compare times. Plutôt can express a preference: Je voudrais plutôt du thé.

concept.line: For things, y can replace à plus the thing: Je pense à ce plan; j'y pense. En can replace de plus the thing: Je parle de ce plan; j'en parle. In Qu'est-ce que tu en penses?, en goes with penser de. For a person, these examples use à elle or de lui. Keep a number with en: J'en ai deux.

concept.line: To ask one familiar person to bring something, say Apporte ta veste. To tell them to take it away with them, say Emporte ta veste. The command has no subject pronoun. S'il te plaît keeps the same familiar register.

concept.line: After a past reporting verb, que introduces a statement and si a yes/no question: Il a dit qu'il était malade; Elle a demandé si tu venais. The imperfect often gives the reported present; had done uses the past perfect, and a future viewed from the past uses the conditional.
